evidence: mux.lisp:304 `(fnn-socket-shut (fnn-mux-conn-socket conn))` (io.lisp:5550 socket-close), and only afterwards mux.lisp:307-311 `(fnn-with-roster (service) (setf (fnn-owner-service-clients service) (delete (fnn-mux-conn-socket conn) ...)))`. The stopper (owner.lisp:1723-1729) copies the clients list and calls `sb-bsd-sockets:socket-shutdown` on each socket, relying on 'Only the worker that cached the socket fd may close it; shutdown wakes its raw read without making that integer available for reuse underneath it.'
failure-message: S084: socket closed while still in the clients roster
fix: Remove the socket from fnn-owner-service-clients under the roster lock before calling fnn-socket-shut, which is the order fnn-socket-shutdown's docstring requires.

reviewer: The ordering inversion is real. fnn-mux-finish calls fnn-socket-shut, which is socket-close (io.lisp:5550-5552), at mux.lisp:304, and removes the socket from clients only afterwards (mux.lisp:307-311). The stopper copies clients and shuts each one down (owner.lisp:1726-1731), relying on the invariant stated at owner.lisp:1723-1725. For the stopper to hit a reused fd, though, it must read the descriptor slot between SBCL's close(2) and its setf of the slot to -1, a few instructions apart, and the kernel must hand that fd out in the same window. New adopts are already refused once stopping is set, so only a feed or file fd could be hit, and only during a stop. Narrow race, low impact. Removing from the roster before closing would make it impossible.
scenario: The loop thread closes fd N in fnn-mux-finish. The accept thread immediately gets fd N for a new client, or a feed opens it. A concurrent stop copies the roster, which still holds the old socket object, and calls shutdown(2) on it. If SBCL's socket-close has not yet cleared the object's descriptor slot, the shutdown hits the new connection's fd N and kills an unrelated session (or a peer feed).
title: fnn-mux-finish closes the socket before removing it from the clients roster, breaking the stop hook's no-fd-reuse invariant
